subject: Silverpine opportunity — capacity guard request and conditional hold
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Silverpine capacity guard request

Team —

Silverpine is in the final legal review for the Dedicated contract (deal SP-2029-041). Legal expects signature within 2–3 weeks, procurement timeline attached separately. Before we push them to sign, they want a stronger signal on capacity availability so their VP of infra is comfortable.

Ask: can ops validate that we can cover a conservative dedicated footprint for their initial rollout and place a conditional soft hold that expires in 60 days? High-level requirements they shared:
- Target throughput: 20,000 tokens/sec peak (inference) across latency-sensitive routes
- Preferred hardware: A100-class, prefer 80GB if possible, fall back to 40GB with quantization plan
- Estimated required sustained capacity (month 1): 8x80GB nodes (estimated 64 A100 GPUs) with headroom for spikes

What I need from you by EOD:
1) Current available pool and any constraints (maintenance windows, thermal binning).
2) Suggested conservative hold quantity and node count we can promise (soft hold id if we can create).
3) Any model/quantization guidance to reduce GPU footprint while meeting latency targets.

I attached their requirements doc for reference. This needs to be precise — Silverpine is sensitive to being overcommitted.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: silverpine_requirements_v2.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Silverpine capacity guard request

Rachel —

Quick snapshot of inventory and constraints (as of this morning):
- Pool A (on-demand/dedicated spare): 120 x A100-80GB equivalent available across us-west and us-central.
- Thermal/affinity: 18% of nodes earmarked for scheduled training jobs (weekly windows Fri 02:00–08:00 UTC) but can be reallocated with 48–72h notice.
- Maintenance: Patch window for us-central hypervisor cluster on 2029-05-18 (4-hour window).

Recommended conservative hold: 10 nodes (40 GPUs A100-80GB equivalent) as a 60-day soft hold. That gives Silverpine ~62% of your stated month-1 ask but is sized to preserve SLOs. If they accept quantization + dynamic batching we can effectively cover their throughput with fewer GPUs:
- Option A (performance-first): 10 x 4-GPU nodes (A100-80GB) — soft hold id: SOFT-HOLD-2791
- Option B (cost-lift, quantized): 7 x 4-GPU nodes (A100-40GB quantized + bf16 kernel) — needs model team signoff but reduces footprint ~30%

I attached a quick capacity_rundown.xlsx with regional distribution and fallback plan. We can set the soft hold now; it won't create billing commitments until they convert to a reserved capacity contract.

Questions:
- Marcus/Neha — any objections on temporary hold ID and expiration policy?
- Rachel — confirm Silverpine is ok with a 60-day soft hold (they mentioned 45–90 days).

Thanks,
Karthik
Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference

Attachments: capacity_rundown.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-11T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Silverpine capacity guard request

All —

Ops can place a conditional soft hold as requested. Notes on policy / implementation:
- Hold ID SOFT-HOLD-2791 created by ops; expires 2029-07-10 23:59 UTC unless converted.
- Hold is per-region; I distributed 6 nodes us-west / 4 nodes us-central (can rebalance if Silverpine needs a specific region).
- We will annotate the hold with minimal commit language for legal: "soft-hold — nonbinding capacity reservation for negotiation period."

Risk items to flag to the customer:
- If production training spikes unexpectedly, we may require 72h notice to maintain the full hold during maintenance windows.
- Thermal binning could reduce usable GPUs by 5–10% in extreme heat cycles; ops will place low-risk nodes for holds.

Action items I will take today:
- Upload internal hold ticket and attach the Silverpine requirements PDF.
- Coordinate with model team to validate quantization path (Neha, can you run a quick eval on 2 representative prompts and share latency delta by EOD?).

Marcus
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: silverpine_requirements_v2.pdf
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@silverpine.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, procurement <procurement@silverpine.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-11T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Silverpine capacity guard request

Rachel / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround — this is helpful. Silverpine can accept a 60-day soft hold as long as we receive:
1) Hold confirmation with an ID we can reference in procurement.
2) A simple nonbinding note that the hold does not create financial obligation until conversion.
3) DocuSign link for the dedicated contract (we need it to start internal approval flows).

Procurement timeline: we can complete internal approval in 10 business days once we have the DocuSign and hold confirmed. We will aim to convert to reserved capacity within 45 days post-signature.

Elena Torres
VP Infrastructure, Silverpine AI
elena.torres@silverpine.ai

Subject: Re: Silverpine capacity guard request — confirmation

Elena —

We added the nonbinding annotation per your ask and attached the hold ticket to the HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/SP-2029-041

DocuSign: sending you the dedicated contract now (link below). Once you start the DocuSign flow we can monitor and prioritize the 48–72h onboarding tasks.
- DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/secure/documents/abc123-silverpine

Neha — any updates on the two prompt evals? If quantization proves viable we will flag Option B to Elena as a path to shrink initial reserved commitment.

Rachel
